DETAILS OF DPWH’s PROGRAMS/PROJECTS 191
PROGRAMS / ACTIVITIES / PROJECTS 
OPERATIONS 
ORGANIZATIONAL OUTCOME 1 : Ensure Safe and Reliable National Road System 
Asset Preservation Program 
The program aims to improve the quality of national roads to international standards and ensure resiliency to natural 
disasters. This program encompasses the preservation of the existing paved national roads through the following sub-
programs: Preventive Maintenance; Rehabilitation/ Reconstruction/Upgrading of damaged paved national roads; 
Rehabilitation/Reconstruction of National Roads with slips, slope collapse, and landslide; construction, 
upgrading/rehabilitation of drainage along national roads. 
Preventive Maintenance 
Preventive maintenance is a sub-program under the Asset Preservation Program that aims to preserve and prolong the 
lifespan of national roads. niis program is typically carried out on roads that are in fair to poor condition, with the 
primary objective of preventing and delaying further deterioration to a state where extensive rehabilitation is 
necessary. Preventive maintenance aims to prevent and delay the deterioration of national roads to a bad condition 
where ultimately rehabilitation is required, which typically involves Asphalt Overlar, Asphalt Overlay with Correction, 
and Concrete Reblocking.Asphalt Overlay is done on roads in fair condition. It involves the application of an additional 
layer of asphalt, that covers imperfections in existing asphalt or concrete. It is commonly applied to pavement that 
hasminor damage like light cracking, mild deterioration, or slightly sunken areas. nie process of overlaying asphalt 
commonly includes a leveling out of the old asphalt pavement, ensuring a smooth, even surface on which to add 
additional layers.Asphalt Overlay with Correction is done on roads in poor condition. It involves the repair of short 
intermittent damaged sections before applying asphalt overlay. For concrete roads, the most common type of 
corrective maintenance is a combination of concrete pavement restoration (CPR) in terms of the replacement of 
intermittent shattered slabs and asphalt overlay.Concrete reblocking is done on national roads in poor condition which 
involves selective reblocking or replacement of intermittent shattered slabs in bad condition. process aims to improve 
the pavement's load-bearing capacity, reduce the risk of potholes, and enhance the pavement's durability and 
longevity.

258 EXPENDITURE PROGRAM FY 2027 VOLUME II-B
PROGRAMS / ACTIVmES / PROJECTS 
Network Deyelopment Program 
The Network Development Program focuses specifically on the expansion and improvement of the national road network.It 
aims to expand the capacity of the national road network by constructing new roads that meet the functional classification 
criteria and improving the quality of existing national roads through various activities. Eligibility for later classification as a 
national road is determined by a feasibility study and the functional classification criteria set by DPWH. This is also achieved 
through a range of activities such as road widening, the construction of bypasses and diversion roads, the construction of 
missing links/new roads, the construction of flyovers, interchanges, underpasses, long-span bridges, off-carriageway 
improvement, and the paving of unpaved roads. The program includes several sub-programs aimed at achieving its 
objectives. These sub-programs include: Road Widening; Construction of By-Passes and Diversion Roads; Construction of 
Missing Links/ New Roads; Construction of Flyovers/ Interchanges/ Underpasses/ Long Span Bridges; Off-Carriageway 
Improvement,· Paving of Unpaved Roads 
Road Widening 
This involves widening the existing road pavement to accommodate more lanes to ease traffic congestion, improve 
traffic now, and increase road capadty. Road widening is essential in high-traffic areas where there is a need to 
increase the capacity of the national road network.

Bridge Program 
The Bridge Program aims to preserve and enhance the existing national bridges and comprises sub-programs such as 
Replacement of bridges (Temporary to Permanent), Replacement of Permanent Weak Bridges, Retrofitting/ Strengthening 
Permanent Bridges, Rehabilitation/ Major Repair of Permanent Bridges, Widening of Permanent Bridges, and Construction of 
New Bridges. 
Replacement of Bridges (Temporary to Permanent} 
This iinvolves replacing temporary bridges made of timber or Bailey materials with permanent structures. These 
temporary bridges have a short life span, limited loading capacity, and speed restrictions.
